source_issue.title: Upgrade test from the last published release, with content checks

summary_markdown:
## What this issue is about
This issue focuses on enhancing our testing process. It involves upgrading to the latest published `plone/plone` release and ensuring that content created before the upgrade remains accessible.

## What needs to be done
1. Install the latest published version of `plone/plone`.
2. Create a webpage that includes an image.
3. Perform a `helm upgrade` to apply the changes from the relevant pull request.
4. Verify that the webpage and image are still functioning correctly after the upgrade. 

**Note:** This task depends on Issue #29 for context and prerequisites.

## Helpful background
Helm is a tool used for managing Kubernetes applications. In this case, it helps us upgrade our Plone application seamlessly. Understanding the basics of Helm and how to set up a Plone environment will be beneficial.

## Good first steps
1. Familiarize yourself with setting up Plone and Helm if you haven’t already.
2. Check out the documentation for the latest `plone/plone` release to see any changes.
3. Look at Issue #29 to grasp the dependencies and context.
4. Start experimenting with creating a page in Plone and performing a Helm upgrade locally to practice those skills.  

Don’t hesitate to ask questions if anything is unclear!
